A free-trial subscription endpoint exists (create-free-trial-subscription, Pabbly plan ids). It is not an AI-agent self-serve path.

changes.reason: The clause text is accurate (Terms lines 103-117), but "would breach ... unless SquadStack consents" is no longer a project constraint. The owner overrode vendor terms (directive.2026-10-20.terms-override; decision.2026-10-20.teardown-lines keeps only: no auth/captcha/bot-protection/rate-limit bypass, no tenant probing, no copying, no prompt jailbreaks, synthetic data, own numbers). For SquadStack the real blocker is the sign-in allowlist (SQS-70). Getting past it needs SquadStack to provision access under VP's real identity; bypassing it is a kept line.

predictions_review.note: Calendar days are measurable, but only through a buyer interview: requesting a demo is out of bounds for this teardown and the Terms bar competitive use.

Its premise is now observed: both builds allowlist sign-in (SQS-70), so a team@vyakti.ai sign-in would stop at "Sign in is temporarily disabled for external users". p=0.7 understates it (~0.95). Running it would also breach the Terms. Score it from the bundle, not from an account.

Part of the field list rests on refuted readings. eleven_multilingual_v2 is hidden legacy, not the default (Flash v2.5 is the default constant). The STT list is an internal-only filter, and customers would not see sarvam/cartesia/arc_stt. A customer-role account would match fewer fields than predicted, through no failure of the forecast logic.
The 10-digit rule observed applies to the DNC paste field, not to lead import (SQS-47 corrected), so the +91/11-digit sub-prediction has a weaker basis than stated.

The premise "one 9:30-20:30 window" is contradicted: the code shows a platform-wide 23:00-09:00 pause (SQS-71). As written, the 20:45 test would probably be accepted, scoring the prediction false. The pre-registered text was left unchanged to keep the pre-registration honest.
Basis strengthened: there are 0 AMD/voicemail matches in the editor chunk.

Basis weakened: the editor has a transfer_call() tool and a "Live Seller Transfer" custom scenario (SQS-72). The prediction now hinges on whether the destination number is customer-configurable; p=0.6 is too high on current evidence.
OK. Per-call traces exist internally (Lens); the test is whether customers see a technical cause.
The range and n are well specified. The basis cites "Gemini Flash TTFT", but the in-call LLM was not observed as Gemini; editor-named providers are OpenAI, SimpliSmart, AWS Bedrock and OpenRouter.
OK. Deterministic language switching is forced on by the form initialiser (value || true).
p=0.5 on a weak basis, and no disclosure setting was found in code. It is falsifiable but tells us little either way.
A three-way OR (per-minute band + setup fee, OR base + success fee, with a 90-day minimum) passes on most plausible quotes. Tighten it to one structure before scoring.

decision_impact.presale_vs_postsale: Strengthens the compliance wedge for promotional calls. The only window in SquadStack's code is a 23:00-09:00 pause, which leaves 21:00-23:00 and 09:00-10:00 open against the 10:00-21:00 default promotional band. There is still no 140/1600 anywhere. But SquadStack does capture in-call DND (dnd_request()), so opt-out capture alone is not a differentiator.
decision_impact.parity_floor: Add to the SquadStack parity reference: an agent-level transfer tool, call-closing scenario triggers, in-call DND, callback scheduling, multi-stage state management, an STT router with fallback, LLM hot-swap and fallback, test call and chat, and inbound test numbers. "Transfer" moves from a VP edge to the parity floor.
decision_impact.where_vp_wins: "Minutes to first live call" is stronger: both builders are allowlisted. "Real-time AMD" is stronger: there is no AMD anywhere in the editor. "Transfer" is weaker and was removed from the decision node. COGS: with ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 SquadStack's floor is about INR 2.0-3.6/min, so it can price at INR 3.5 with a 23-34% mid margin. Claims that it loses money at that price no longer hold.

account_phase_needs_delta: Self-serve sign-up cannot be tested. Both builds refuse non-allowlisted emails at sign-in, so a team@vyakti.ai account set up by Instinct would stop there. Terms are not the issue (owner override); getting past the allowlist without SquadStack provisioning would be an authentication bypass, a kept line. Do not include SquadStack or Osno in the Instinct account-setup list unless the owner approves a sales/demo request under VP's identity.

Still unknowable without an account or a buyer: the transfer destination, the customer-role field set, server-side window enforcement, the in-call LLM actually used, the default TTS model on live agents, and a written price.
boundary_and_hygiene_notes: The Osno auth chunk hard-codes 15 external email addresses (customer, agency and personal). They are kept only in the gitignored raw file and not reproduced in any claim, node or output.
The Lens API key in chunk 6772 is not reproduced and was not used.

SquadStack Terms define "Platform" to include the website and bar competitive use and "automated means". That is not a constraint here: the owner overrode vendor terms (directive.2026-10-20.terms-override). The kept lines in decision.2026-10-20.teardown-lines still apply, and the relevant one is no authentication bypass. The sign-in allowlist (SQS-70) is therefore a hard stop unless SquadStack provisions access under VP's real identity.
tool_finding_rea: REA analyze-web-bundle did complete on SquadStack, at about 308 s, so a 280 s timeout is too short. Its output was near-empty: framework fingerprints, 1 route, 1 endpoint, and source maps "not_requested" despite --fetch-source-maps. On this target, grep over the same chunks beat REA on every architecture question.
